paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The chart is a donut chart comparing the distribution of samples across different values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The chart has two rings, each with four slices, totaling eight categories. The outer ring represents Ambiguity Std with four slices labeled Std: 0.0 (dark blue, 49.0%), Std: 0.47 (blue, 38.0%), Std: 0.82 (light blue, 7.0%), and Std: 0.94 (pale blue, 5.0%). The inner ring represents Max Ambiguity with three slices labeled Max: 1 (light blue, 39.0%), Max: 2 (pale blue, 47.7%), and Max: 3 (very pale blue, 14.2%). The chart includes a legend for both rings, and percentage labels are displayed inside each slice. The slices are visually ordered from largest to smallest in both rings.
